info.name: FHIR REST API
info.description:
End-to-end tests for the Python FastAPI FHIR R5 REST server.

Run the full collection in order — Auth registers a unique user and saves a Bearer token, which all subsequent requests inherit. The Patient folder creates a resource whose ID is stored in `patientId` and used by Read, History, Observation, and clinical-resource requests. The Sort folder seeds additional patients to verify `_sort` ordering.

**Base URL:** `http://localhost:8000`  
**Auth:** JWT Bearer (token saved automatically after Login)

item.name: Public
item.description: Unauthenticated endpoints. No Authorization header required. Use these to verify the server is running before attempting any authenticated requests.

item.name: Auth
item.description: User registration and login. Register generates a unique username (`alice_<timestamp>`) to avoid conflicts on repeated runs. Login saves the returned JWT to the `token` collection variable, which all protected requests use via `Bearer {{token}}`.

item.name: Patient
item.description: Full CRUD lifecycle for a Patient resource. Create saves the new resource ID to `patientId`, which Read, Update, Patch, and Delete all reference. Run these in order: Create → Read → Search → PUT → PATCH → Delete. The DELETE at the end tombstones the resource so History requests can demonstrate the deleted version.

item.name: History
item.description: Version history interactions. Reads instance, type, and system history bundles. Run after the Patient CRUD folder — the patient will have been created, updated twice (PUT + PATCH), and deleted, so the history bundle should contain at least 3 entries. Version 1 may return 410 Gone after the DELETE.

item.name: Observation
item.description: Search interactions for Observation resources. Demonstrates subject reference filtering, LOINC code filtering, date range filtering with `ge`/`le` prefixes, and pagination via `_count`/`_offset`. These requests return empty bundles if no Observations have been created — that is still a valid 200 searchset response.

item.name: Condition, AllergyIntolerance, MedicationRequest
item.description: Search interactions for common clinical resources linked to the patient. All three filter by subject/patient reference using `patientId`. Empty bundles are expected unless matching resources have been created separately — the tests only assert on the Bundle structure, not entry count.

item.name: Sort
item.description: Validates `_sort` query parameter support. Two seed patients (Adams and Carter) are created first to guarantee the result set contains sortable data. All three sort requests use `_count=10` to avoid fetching thousands of records. Assertions check relative ordering of consecutive entries rather than hardcoded names, so they pass regardless of what other data is in the database.

item.name: Errors
item.description: Negative-path tests that verify correct error responses. Covers missing token (401), invalid token (401), wrong password (401), unknown resource type (404), and wrong Content-Type on PATCH (415). All responses are asserted to be OperationOutcome resources.
